title: Expeditio Persica, Bellum Avaricum, Heraclias (+ Hexaemeron); «Ираклиада», «На нашествие варваров» и др.
author: George of Pisidia
genre: Panegyrical epic in iambic trimeter; didactic-theological poem (Hexaemeron)
size: About 5,000 verses in total. Expeditio Persica 1,088; Bellum Avaricum about 540; Heraclias about 470; Hexaemeron about 1,900 (approximate).
edition: Pertusi 1959; Tartaglia 1998 (UTET, complete); Gonnelli 1998 (Hexaemeron). Public-domain texts: Bekker, CSHB 1836; Querci 1777 = PG 92 (scans; URLs not checked).
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Георгий Писида' lists only Russian 'отрывки' (excerpts) of Expeditio Persica, Bellum Avaricum, Heraclias and others. Hexaemeron is not listed.
en_evidence: No complete English translation found on English Wikipedia or Crossref; only studies (Whitby, Howard-Johnston, Leppin).
value: Eyewitness court poetry on Heraclius' Persian war, the Avar-Persian siege of Constantinople (626) and the True Cross. Used as a source by Theophanes. The last classicizing panegyric of Late Antiquity, at the 7th-century cutoff. Hexaemeron is a key text on late-antique science and Platonism.
ai_feasibility: Medium-high. The trimeters are dense and allusive, with rare vocabulary. Italian translations allow cross-checking, and historical commentary can draw on Howard-Johnston.
pilot_unit: Bellum Avaricum (about 540 lines, the 626 siege), then Expeditio Persica
